sourceChecks.title: Brain-computer Interfaces for Communication in Patients with Disorders of Consciousness: a Gap Analysis and Scientific Roadmap
sourceChecks.locator: Section “Non-invasive vs. invasive signal acquisition,” pp. 13–14
sourceChecks.excerpt: The ideal technique would be non-invasive, have high spatial and temporal resolution
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A review/roadmap contrasts scalp EEG resolution with invasive recordings and explicitly lists the desired non-invasive high-resolution signal as a research need.
sourceChecks.limitations: The review concerns communication in patients with disorders of consciousness; it does not demonstrate single-neuron non-invasive, bidirectional, safe, zero-training BCI.

sourceChecks.title: Future of AR display: Holographic contact lens
sourceChecks.excerpt: a significant limitation in AR contact lenses is the inability of the eyes to focus
sourceChecks.paraphrase: The perspective describes existing contact-lens display prototypes and the image-formation/focus challenges still under research.
sourceChecks.limitations: Not a perfected all-day display; reported prototypes have limited field of view and unresolved focus/transparency issues; does not establish zero latency.

sourceChecks.title: Facial Expression Recognition with Controlled Privacy Preservation and Feature Compensation
sourceChecks.excerpt: 78.84% recognition accuracy with a privacy leakage ratio of only 2.01%
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A closed-set CREMA-D experiment balances facial-expression recognition and identity privacy; reported accuracy is 78.84% and identity leakage 2.01%.
sourceChecks.limitations: Closed-set benchmark, 91 identities and identity-only privacy; not multimodal universal emotion/intention recognition, perfect accuracy, consent, or zero privacy invasion.

sourceChecks.title: Adapting User Interfaces with Model-based Reinforcement Learning
sourceChecks.excerpt: outperforms both a non-adaptive and a frequency-based policy
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Model-based RL plans adaptive-menu changes and reports empirical and simulated performance better than non-adaptive/frequency policies in that task.
sourceChecks.limitations: Results are for adaptive menus and do not show open-ended anticipation of users’ needs, self-evolution, or zero-effort general interfaces.

sourceChecks.title: An Overview of Wearable Haptic Technologies and Their Performance in Virtual Object Exploration
sourceChecks.excerpt: The lack of general testing methods for object exploration
sourceChecks.paraphrase: The review maps user-tested wearable haptic devices; only 13 studies addressed user-testing in healthy subjects and general testing methods were lacking.
sourceChecks.limitations: Wearable haptics reproduce selected cues/tasks, not the full range of tactile, thermal and proprioceptive sensations with universal fidelity.

sourceChecks.title: Adaptive User Interfaces for People with Cognitive Disabilities within the Easy Reading Framework
sourceChecks.excerpt: dynamically adapt to the users’ preferences and abilities
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Easy Reading describes adaptive/adjustable tools for cognitive web accessibility; the paper also notes tradeoffs and consistency risks.
sourceChecks.limitations: Covers web-page reading/accessibility and available features, not automatic accessibility for every sensory/cognitive ability or proof across all interfaces.

sourceChecks.title: Websites Need Your Permission Too – User Sentiment and Decision Making on Web Permission Prompts in Desktop Chrome
sourceChecks.excerpt: using 28 days of telemetry data from more than 100M Chrome installations
sourceChecks.paraphrase: A CHI study analyzes 28-day telemetry from over 100M Chrome installs and survey/experience responses from 25,706 users; prompt dismissal/ignoring was common for geolocation and notifications.
sourceChecks.limitations: This evaluates browser permission prompts, not strong end-to-end privacy guarantees or zero effort/cognitive load for privacy management.

sourceChecks.title: Investigating co-presence and collaboration dynamics in realtime virtual reality user interactions
sourceChecks.excerpt: voice communication significantly improved the efficiency of task performance
sourceChecks.paraphrase: The paper reviews prior VR work and reports its own controlled user study of avatar/voice factors; communication and rendering factors affect co-presence/collaboration.
sourceChecks.limitations: A bounded VR task with measured presence/task outcomes does not establish remote co-location indistinguishability or universal fidelity of gaze, spatial audio, and presence.

sourceChecks.title: Man-Computer Symbiosis
sourceChecks.excerpt: At present, however, there are no man-computer symbioses.
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Licklider presents human-computer symbiosis as a prospective research development and says no man-computer symbioses yet existed at the time of writing.
sourceChecks.limitations: A 1960 vision paper is not a contemporary predictive law or a validated universal theory of optimal human-AI collaboration.

sourceChecks.title: Design for Long-term Memory Augmentation in Personal Knowledge Management Applications
sourceChecks.excerpt: users rarely revisit their digitally saved content
sourceChecks.paraphrase: Survey and focus group report that users rarely revisit saved PKM content and propose reminder-based memory augmentation design principles.
sourceChecks.limitations: Small studies (survey N=58, focus group N=7) propose future designs; they do not demonstrate lifelong seamless integration, recall accuracy, security, or cognitive fit.
